propositions: Compaction writes SNAPSHOT.json and *.retired, then commits non-atomically in a detached worker; if the worker is killed before commit, the working tree is left dirty with untracked files.
When reconverge runs git merge origin/tickets, those same paths now exist on origin (pushed by a peer clone); git aborts with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge'.

The abort handler in _union_merge and push_recovery cannot clear untracked files (git reset --hard is tracked-only, git stash without -u does not capture them), so every retry re-aborts identically, wedging the store and stranding local commits off origin.

The fix detects the untracked-overwrite abort signature, parses the exact paths git names, relocates only those paths to a quarantine directory outside the worktree, and retries the merge once; on success, both parents are kept and no local commit is orphaned.
On any other failure or genuine conflict, the abort-only behavior is preserved unchanged (git merge --abort, keep local, log fsck-recover hint).
Defense-in-depth follow-up: make compaction crash-atomic (roll back the dirty tree on worker death) so the dirty state is not produced in the first place.
